328: Discussion. Iron deficiency is the commonest nutritional disorder among rice-eating populations, so that the iron retained in the product is of direct importance and a higher content is preferable. Grain iron is contingent upon the quantity remobilised from the flag leaf and upon the chelators effecting its transport, both of which differ between cultivars, while cooking translocates a proportion of it inward from the pericarp.
329: The same pattern has been reported previously. Sonu et al. (2025) determined that grain iron is heritable but that few lines attain nutritional targets; Kumar et al. (2022) that iron migrates inward and becomes more available; Jannasch and Wang (2020) that the steep water may convey iron and calcium into the endosperm; and Akter et al. (2025) that iron declined while protein and zinc were concentrated. The leading cultivar varied with the product, Gobindabhog and Harinakhuri ranking highest in turn, so that no single recommendation covers the group on this attribute.

335: Discussion. Zinc is required for immune function, growth and wound healing, and after iron is the mineral most frequently deficient in rice-based diets, so that a higher content is preferable. Zinc loading is contingent upon the HMA2 and HMA4 transporters and upon remobilisation during grain filling, the element being retained in the aleurone largely as phytate salts.
336: Earlier reports corroborate this finding. Kumar et al. (2022) determined that zinc migrates outward on treatment, unlike iron; Sonu et al. (2025) that grain zinc is polygenic with wide genotypic variance; Hu et al. (2019) that zinc is retained in the germ and aleurone; and Oliveira et al. (2026) that polishing is of greater consequence than the thermal step. The leading position was shared between Gobindabhog, Kalojira and Kataribhog, so that selection on this attribute must be made product by product.

342: Discussion. Manganese is required by superoxide dismutase and certain other enzymes. The dietary requirement is small, but cereals supply the greater part of it, so that a higher content is preferable. Manganese enters through NRAMP and MTP transporters and accumulates in the aleurone, so that the value is contingent upon uptake and upon the proportion of the outer grain surviving milling.

350: Discussion. Lightness measures the degree to which the product has remained pale. It declines with browning and with the inward migration of pigments, so that a higher value generally denotes gentler processing. Lightness declines as browning products accumulate and as pericarp pigments dissolve and migrate inward, and cultivars richer in reducing sugar and free amino nitrogen brown further under an identical treatment.
351: Comparable observations appear in the literature. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that darkening proceeds from pigment migration and browning; Srisang et al. (2021) that lightness declines as the thermal treatment becomes more severe; Panda et al. (2021) that shorter heating yields a lighter product at equivalent moisture loss; and Akter et al. (2025) that a darker product was nonetheless preferred overall. No single cultivar proved superior across all the products: Dudeshwar and Kataribhog ranked highest in different ones, so that the decision is contingent upon the product concerned.

357: Discussion. The a* value is signed: a positive value places the sample on the red side of the green-to-red axis and a negative value on the green side. Redness increases as browning proceeds, so that a lower value is preferred. Redness rises as melanoidins and their coloured precursors accumulate, the rate being contingent upon the reducing sugars and free amino acids the cultivar supplies.
358: Previous studies describe the same behaviour. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that the amber shift proceeds from Maillard browning; Srisang et al. (2021) that colour develops with time and temperature; Ayamdoo et al. (2014) that the extent of colour development is cultivar-specific; and Panda et al. 364: Discussion. Yellowness arises from the migration of bran pigments into the endosperm and from early browning products. Except where a golden colour is required, a lower value is preferable. It derives from carotenoids and flavonoids conveyed inward from the pericarp during hydration together with early browning products, so that cultivars richer in pigment return higher values.
365: Earlier work is largely concordant. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that bran pigments dissolve on soaking and are fixed on drying; Srisang et al. (2021) that yellowing is proportional to the heat load; Devi and Badwaik (2022) that colour readings track pigment composition; and Oliveira et al. (2026) that final colour is contingent upon pigment and processing jointly. The leading cultivar varied with the product, Radhatilak and Tulaipanjii ranking highest in turn, so that no single recommendation covers the group on this attribute.

371: Discussion. This parameter measures the overall colour distance between the product and the raw grain; a smaller value denotes that the grain has altered in texture without appreciable alteration in appearance. It integrates all three colour coordinates and therefore registers both pigment migration and browning, each of which scales with the substrate the cultivar provides.
372: This is consistent with previous studies. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that colour constitutes the principal barrier to the acceptance of processed rice; Srisang et al. (2021) that a combined colour index discriminates between treatments more effectively than any single axis; Panda et al. (2021) that equivalent processing may be achieved at a smaller colour cost; and Akter et al. (2025) that overall colour change corresponded to the panel's judgement. The leading position was shared between Kataribhog and Tulaipanjii, so that selection on this attribute must be made product by product.

379: Discussion. Aroma distinguishes the traditional aromatic cultivars from ordinary grain and arises principally from 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline, so that a higher score is unambiguously preferable. This compound accumulates where the BADH2 gene is non-functional and its precursor is free to cyclise; being volatile, it is likewise sensitive to thermal exposure.
